name: Going Down

voices._why: the owner-approved Grand Central sample (21 Nov 2026) used am_michael at speed 1.3; the owner said 'great, I like this' and made it the channel

_numbersWhy: depths, lengths, times and counts from sourced facts; metres computed from feet (or feet from metres) in code, never typed
disclaimer: Depths from published sources. Cutaway illustrations, not to scale.

look._why: owner-approved sample: one continuous flat 2D cutaway, the camera dives straight down through the real layers under a famous place, a depth meter in ft and m, each layer landing on its word, a pull-back reveal, then the ride back up into frame 1 (loop). Kit: remotion/src/dive (README) on remotion/src/flat
look.style: flat ink-outlined cross-section: the landmark above ground, coloured soil and rock strata below, lit tunnels and rooms cut into the rock, trains and riders moving, a station-style sign with the depth on every layer, a depth meter on the left, big white caption words with figures in yellow

rotation._why: every video must look new (CLAUDE.md variety rules): the sky/time of day, the strata palette and the landmark facade change per video; never the same palette as the last 3

_uploadCategoryWhy: 27 Education: how places are built underneath, from published sources

length._why: owner, 21 Nov: 20-25 s Shorts; the approved sample is 22.0 s; scan's 20-35 s band had the best median (184,772 views)

cadence._why: owner, 21 Nov: 3 Shorts a day, no long videos

samples._why: owner, 21 Nov: the Grand Central sample is the approval; no further samples, straight to review

voiceSpeed._why: the approved sample: am_michael at 1.3 put 7 lines (~70 words) into 22 s

beatPad._why: the approved sample ran the narration on with almost no pause between layers (70 words in 22 s); the platform 0.35 s + 0.5 s a beat made the first Short 28 s (2026-11-21)

likeness._why: the sample is the reference: ~190 words a minute, a new layer every ~2.5 s

motion._why: the sample lands a new layer every 1.5-4.5 s and something always moves (trains, riders, taxis, lamps)

sound._why: the approved sample: a low muted pulse under the voice, a whoosh on every dive, a water/air rush into the deepest level, one sub-boom on the payoff, a thud on the loop. Uses the shared cinematic bed (not another channel's own beds)

note: Written by the /new-channel build phase (fast path, owner 21 Nov: scan + the approved sample, no full research). generator/pack.py reads it.
